title: "I will tell you the most secret" (9.1–9.10)
hook: Krishna promises the royal secret, and it turns out to be a riddle about where the world lives
tomorrow: The one who offers a leaf (9.11–9.25)

segments.voice: Yesterday, uttarayana: the day and night of Brahma, and the path of light and the path of smoke. Your line was the two paths. Today, the end of the week, and chapter nine begins.

Krishna leans in, the way a friend does when the room goes quiet, and says: I'm going to tell you the most secret thing. Because you don't sneer. It's been a week of big ideas: one in a thousand, the world strung like pearls on a thread, four kinds of devotees, all noble, maya, the veil, what is Brahman, and remember me, the last thought, the day and night of Brahma. And still, everybody leans in for a secret. So what is it?
screen: `THE ROOM GOES QUIET.` → `A WEEK OF BIG IDEAS.` → `THE MOST SECRET THING.`

segments.voice: Verse one: to you, who doesn't find fault, I'll tell the most secret knowledge, together with its realization. Verse two gives it a grand name: raja-vidya, raja-guhya. The king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the highest purifier. Then three surprising words: it's known directly, by experience; it's in line with dharma; and it's easy to practice. The deepest secret in the Gita is called easy. Here it is. Verse four: all this world is pervaded by me, in my unseen form. All beings rest in me, but I don't rest in them. Verse five turns it over: and yet beings don't rest in me either. Behold my divine power. It's a riddle, on purpose. Verse six gives a picture to hold it: as the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in me. The wind moves; space doesn't. The wind is in space, but space isn't pushed around by it, or used up by it. So everything is in Krishna, and nothing contains or disturbs him. Then yesterday's cycle comes back: at the end of an age all beings go into my nature, and at the beginning I send them forth again. Those actions don't bind me, verse nine says; I sit as if unconcerned, unattached. Verse ten: under my eye, nature brings forth the moving and the unmoving, and the world turns. That's the royal secret, as the Gita tells it: you're already inside the one you're looking for, like wind inside the sky.
screen: `THE KING OF SECRETS.` · `KNOWN DIRECTLY, EASY TO PRACTICE.` · `ALL BEINGS REST IN ME.` · `LIKE WIND IN THE SKY.` · then, large: `YOU'RE ALREADY INSIDE.`

segments.voice: Picture a wide, open sky with wind moving through it, some gusts strong, some gentle, and let your thoughts be the wind. Each time a thought gusts through, notice the space it moves in. You don't need to stop the wind; the sky doesn't mind it, so just rest as the sky.
Raja-guhya. The royal secret, the king of secrets. Gita nine: all beings rest in God, as wind rests in the sky.
Your line: the secret. The wind moves, and the sky holds it without being moved. That's day one hundred eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Chapter nine, the raja-vidya raja-guhya yoga, is one of the most loved chapters of the Gita; many Hindus read it for its teaching that all beings rest in God and that devotion is easy and open to all.

fork.setup: Krishna needs a picture for how all beings can rest in him without touching him. which does he use?
fork.reveal: wind in space, verse 6. the great wind moves everywhere and always rests in space, which isn't moved by it.

original.note: Sanskrit: raja-guhya, the royal secret; guhya, secret, from guh, to hide.

trapdoor: what you thought: a secret means something hidden from most people.
what it means: the king of secrets is right in front of you, known directly and easy to practice: all beings rest in God, like wind in the sky.

what a scholar hears: guhya comes from guh, to hide, the root of guha, a cave; 9.4–5's paradox (beings are in me, yet not in me) is called 'my divine yoga', and the wind-in-space image of 9.6 is how the Gita resolves it.
recall: my dear, said by an elder to a child
